name: The Night Regulator
recognitionLine: I use the screen so I do not have to be alone with my head at night.
read: You're someone who can hold it together during the day, but the night is harder. When everything finally goes quiet, the screen becomes the thing that turns the volume down on the thoughts you didn't get to during the day. It's less about what's on the screen and more about not having to be alone with your head before sleep.
definition: A pre-sleep loop where the screen becomes an off-switch for rumination, dread, loneliness, or quiet.
thisIsMe: During the day, I can usually keep moving. At night, when the room gets quiet, everything I kept away starts getting louder. My phone is the thing that softens it. I tell myself I just need something on until I am sleepy, then I look up and it is much later than I meant. It is not always fun. It is the thing that keeps me from lying there with my own head.
whatItsDoing: It is giving me a fast way to lower the volume on thoughts, dread, loneliness, or the exposed feeling that shows up when nothing else is happening.
whatItsCosting: Sleep goes first, then mood, focus, patience, appetite, and the next day's ability to handle stress.
whenAdaptive: Wanting help winding down is normal. Screens can sometimes provide comfort, sound, or company during a hard night.
whenProblem: It becomes a problem when the screen is the only off-switch, sleep keeps shrinking, and morning starts paying for what night could not hold.
whatHelps: Replace the off-switch before removing it. Build a wind-down that meets the actual night feeling: sound without scrolling, a written worry dump, low-stakes connection, light movement, or a planned stop point.
firstTinyStep: Tonight, choose one non-feed off-switch before bed and put the phone out of reach after one planned stop point.
evidenceLabel: Supported inference; sleep regulation and bedtime smartphone-use literature
coreSignals: Late-night or in-bed use; time-sink after intended bedtime; uses content as sedation more than entertainment; dread, rumination, loneliness, or silence before use; tired and dysregulated mornings.
differentiators: Separate from The Time Reclaimer by function. Night Regulator is about not being alone with inner noise. Time Reclaimer is about reclaiming personal freedom.
deeperPattern: Sleep procrastination, emotion regulation, negative reinforcement, and compensatory media use. Keep diagnostic claims out unless impairment is clinically assessed.
scoringNotes: High fit when Night Regulation plus Zone-Out or Companion plus sleep cost is present. Stronger if user reports dread, rumination, loneliness, or numbness before sleep.
avoidSaying: Do not say the user lacks discipline, is addicted to blue light, or just needs better sleep hygiene. The loop is serving a real regulation need.

name: The Time Reclaimer
recognitionLine: I stay up because this is the only part of the day that feels like mine.
read: You're someone who gives all day to other people, and the night is the first stretch that feels like yours. Staying up isn't really about the phone, it's about keeping a piece of the day nobody else gets to claim. The catch is that the freedom comes straight out of tomorrow's energy.
definition: A late-night freedom loop where screens become stolen personal time after a day of obligation, control, work, parenting, school, or pressure.
thisIsMe: All day I am answering to something: work, school, family, messages, responsibilities, other people's needs. Then night comes and nobody is asking anything of me. I know I should sleep, but stopping feels like giving away the only time that belongs to me. So I keep watching, scrolling, playing, reading, or chatting, even when I am exhausted. Part of me knows tomorrow will hurt. Another part of me thinks, at least this part was mine.
whatItsDoing: It is giving me agency, privacy, decompression, and a feeling of ownership over my life when the day felt claimed by everyone else.
whatItsCosting: It buys freedom with sleep. The next day starts depleted, which can make life feel even more controlled and create the same need again at night.
whenAdaptive: The need is healthy. People need unclaimed time, play, privacy, and moments that are not productive or demanded.
whenProblem: It becomes a problem when the only way to feel free is to steal from sleep, health, or the next day's capacity.
whatHelps: Protect personal time earlier in the day, even in small pieces. Make the night ritual feel less like surrender and more like choosing tomorrow's energy for yourself.
firstTinyStep: Put a 20-minute 'mine' block on tomorrow's calendar before night arrives.
evidenceLabel: Supported inference; bedtime procrastination and agency-restoration frame
coreSignals: Late-night use despite exhaustion; day felt externally controlled; use feels like freedom, privacy, or rebellion; sleep loss with a next-day cost; less dread than Night Regulator.
differentiators: Separate from The Night Regulator. Time Reclaimer is about lost autonomy and stolen freedom, not primarily rumination or dread.
deeperPattern: Revenge bedtime procrastination, agency restoration, self-control depletion, and compensation for over-structured days.
scoringNotes: High fit when Night Regulation co-occurs with language about 'my time,' freedom, privacy, control, exhaustion, or resentment.
avoidSaying: Do not frame as childish revenge, laziness, or bad sleep hygiene. The key need is legitimate personal time.

name: The Autopilot Drifter
recognitionLine: I did not choose it. My hand just went there, and now the time is gone.
read: You're someone whose hand finds the phone before you've even decided to reach for it, usually in the small gaps, waiting, walking, switching tasks. It's rarely exciting and rarely a big deal in the moment, it just quietly fills the space. The cost shows up later, in the time and focus that slipped away in pieces.
definition: An automatic gap-filling loop where use happens in transitions, pauses, and small empty spaces without a clear decision or much enjoyment.
thisIsMe: There is a little blank moment: between tasks, waiting for something, walking somewhere, sitting down, waking up, going to the bathroom. Before I have even decided what I want, I am already on the phone. It does not feel exciting. It is just what my hand does. Sometimes I come to and realize I have been gone for twenty minutes, or an hour, and the thing I meant to do has quietly slipped away.
whatItsDoing: It is smoothing over tiny moments of friction, boredom, restlessness, and task-starting discomfort. It removes the empty space before I can feel it.
whatItsCosting: Time disappears in pieces. Attention gets chopped up. Small intentions leak away before they become actions.
whenAdaptive: Brief breaks, boredom relief, and idle scrolling can be harmless. Not every gap needs to be optimized.
whenProblem: It becomes a problem when use is mostly automatic, rarely satisfying, and repeatedly interrupts the next thing I meant to do.
whatHelps: Create a choice point. Add friction, name what each gap is for, and put one better default within reach before the phone becomes the default.
firstTinyStep: Pick one daily gap, like bathroom, elevator, or first five minutes after work, and make it phone-free with a visible cue.
evidenceLabel: BLH formulation; supported by habit, automaticity, and problematic-use models
coreSignals: No clear decision point; transition and waiting moments; autopilot opening; joyless or numb use; time loss without a dramatic trigger; low insight at first.
differentiators: Separate from Night Regulator by timing and from Reward Chaser by affect. Drifter is low-charge, automatic, and often joyless.
deeperPattern: Habit loops, cue-triggered behavior, low-friction design, and negative reinforcement through avoidance of micro-discomfort.
scoringNotes: High fit when Autopilot Loop plus Gap Filling or Anytime / No Pattern appears with low enjoyment and time/focus cost.
avoidSaying: Do not call it addiction by default. Do not overdramatize. The quietness of the loop is the point.

name: The Competence Refuge
recognitionLine: I go where effort turns into progress, because out here I feel behind before I start.
read: You're someone who likes effort that actually adds up, where you can see the level, the rank, the progress. When the rest of life feels uncertain or like you're behind, you go where you can feel capable again. The bind is that the thing you're stepping away from tends to get heavier the longer you're gone.
definition: A competence-escape loop where games, rankings, streaks, creator systems, stats, or digital projects provide clear progress when offline life feels uncertain or defeating.
thisIsMe: In there, effort makes sense. I can see the level, the rank, the streak, the progress bar, the next objective. Out here, I can work hard and still not know if it matters. When school, work, health, money, or life starts making me feel like I am failing, I go where the rules are clear and I can feel capable again. The painful part is that the thing I avoid keeps getting worse, which makes the refuge feel even more necessary.
whatItsDoing: It is restoring competence, control, and proof that my effort can still matter.
whatItsCosting: The avoided offline domain decays: work, school, health, relationships, chores, or finances. Then the failure feeling gets stronger.
whenAdaptive: Mastery, games, stats, and skill-building can be confidence-building, social, creative, and genuinely healthy.
whenProblem: It becomes a problem when the competence space is used right when a hard offline task is due, and the offline task keeps shrinking or worsening.
whatHelps: Do not just remove the one place I feel capable. Build small offline wins, shrink avoided tasks, and treat ADHD, depression, anxiety, or burnout if they are part of the loop.
firstTinyStep: Before entering the refuge, do five minutes of the avoided task with the goal of starting, not finishing.
evidenceLabel: Supported inference; competence, gaming, and compensatory-use frame
coreSignals: Clear digital progress or mastery; offline domain feels vague, humiliating, or impossible; use spikes before hard tasks; irritability when interrupted; avoided responsibilities worsen.
differentiators: Separate from Second Self. Competence Refuge is about winning, progress, and capability. Second Self is about identity and inhabiting another version of self.
deeperPattern: Compensatory internet use, competence restoration, self-efficacy, behavioral activation, and gaming-disorder signals only when impairment and control loss are high.
scoringNotes: High fit when Climb plus Task Avoidance plus responsibility cost appears. Stronger when user names failing, falling behind, mastery, ranking, levels, streaks, or progress.
avoidSaying: Do not shame gaming, fandom, productivity, or skill spaces. Do not imply the person is only escaping. This may be the one place they still feel effective.

name: The Optimizer Spiral
recognitionLine: I keep getting ready to start, but the preparing becomes the thing.
read: You're someone who wants to do it right, so you research, plan, and get set up before you start. It feels responsible, and a lot of the time it is. The trap is when preparing quietly becomes the thing you do instead of starting.
definition: A preparation loop where research, planning, AI, productivity tools, self-improvement, or learning gives a feeling of progress while delaying the real action.
thisIsMe: I am not exactly wasting time. I am researching, planning, watching the tutorial, asking AI, comparing tools, organizing the system, saving the thread, refining the prompt. It feels responsible because I am preparing. But somehow preparing keeps replacing doing. The more I learn, the more ways there are to do it wrong. I end up with more tabs, more notes, more options, and the same thing still not started.
whatItsDoing: It is giving me the feeling of control and competence before I risk doing the real thing imperfectly.
whatItsCosting: Action gets delayed. Confidence drops. The task grows larger in my head because every extra input adds another possible standard.
whenAdaptive: Research, planning, learning, and AI support can be genuinely useful, especially for complex tasks.
whenProblem: It becomes a problem when each extra source makes action less likely, and preparation becomes a safer substitute for starting.
whatHelps: Define enough before you begin. Time-box input, choose a messy first version, and require one action before the next search, prompt, video, or tool.
firstTinyStep: Write the smallest next action, set a 12-minute timer, and do it before opening another source.
evidenceLabel: Emerging BLH frame; uncertainty, preparation, and avoidance loop
coreSignals: Research or AI use before action; many tabs/tools/templates; completion loop around learning or setup; task avoidance masked as responsibility; uncertainty increases with more information.
differentiators: Separate from Vigilant Scanner. Optimizer Spiral is about performing readiness and avoiding imperfect action. Vigilant Scanner is about safety and threat certainty.
deeperPattern: Intolerance of uncertainty, perfectionism, avoidance, productivity theater, and AI-assisted reassurance when tools are used to delay commitment.
scoringNotes: High fit when Rabbit Hole or Companion co-occurs with Task Avoidance, Completion Loop, and work or school cost. Look for 'preparing,' 'researching,' 'optimizing,' or 'not ready.'
avoidSaying: Do not mock self-improvement or productivity tools. Do not say the person is procrastinating as a character flaw.

name: The Reassurance Checker
recognitionLine: I just need to see if something changed, then I can relax. Except I can't.
read: You're someone who checks to make sure nothing's changed and nothing's been missed, and for a second it helps. The relief just doesn't last very long. Checking settles the moment, but it slowly teaches you to check again.
definition: A short-check loop where messages, notifications, replies, views, location, status, or device signals briefly lower anxiety and train the next check.
thisIsMe: It starts as a little pulse. Maybe someone replied. Maybe something changed. Maybe I missed something. Maybe I should know before it gets worse. I check, and for a second my body relaxes. But the relief never lasts long. A few minutes later, the question is back. When I cannot check, part of me stays with the phone anyway.
whatItsDoing: It is trying to give me certainty, social safety, and the relief of knowing I am not missing something important.
whatItsCosting: Focus and sleep get fragmented. Anxiety learns to ask for more checks. Being away from the device starts feeling harder than it should.
whenAdaptive: Checking can be reasonable when timing matters, people depend on me, or I am waiting on something important.
whenProblem: It becomes a problem when the relief is brief, the checking gets more frequent, and not checking feels physically uncomfortable.
whatHelps: Stretch the gap gently. Reduce unnecessary notification cues, set check windows, and work with the fear the check is trying to quiet.
firstTinyStep: Choose one 15-minute no-check window today and let the urge rise and fall without proving anything.
evidenceLabel: Supported inference; FoMO, checking, and reassurance-loop literature
coreSignals: Short frequent checks; notification, reply, view, status, or location monitoring; relief after checking; anxiety during separation; worse during work, class, night, or downtime.
differentiators: Separate from Vigilant Scanner by duration and object. Reassurance Checker is quick signal-checking. Vigilant Scanner is extended research or threat scanning.
deeperPattern: Reassurance seeking, FoMO, checking loops, negative reinforcement, and intolerance of uncertainty. Keep OCD language internal unless clinically appropriate.
scoringNotes: High fit when Tethered Check plus Quick-Check or Waiting / Refresh appears with anxiety relief and focus/sleep cost.
avoidSaying: Do not say OCD-style in user-facing copy. Do not shame responsiveness. Do not imply every check is irrational.

name: The Vigilant Scanner
recognitionLine: If I read enough, maybe I will finally feel safe.
read: You're someone who wants to feel sure before you can rest, so you keep reading, searching, and refreshing until it feels safe. The hope is that one more source will finally settle it. Often the searching keeps the worry awake instead of putting it to sleep.
definition: An uncertainty loop where searching, refreshing, researching, and threat-scanning promise certainty but keep the worry alive.
thisIsMe: There is a symptom, a headline, a decision, a risk, a rumor, a weird feeling, a thing I might be missing. I tell myself I just need one more source, one more thread, one more explanation, one more update. Stopping before I feel sure feels irresponsible. But the more I read, the more there is to worry about, and the point where I am allowed to stop keeps moving.
whatItsDoing: It is trying to turn uncertainty into safety. The real prize is not information, it is the feeling that I can finally stand down.
whatItsCosting: Anxiety grows instead of settling. Hours disappear. Decisions stall because there is always one more thing to check.
whenAdaptive: Research can protect me, help me make better choices, and keep me informed when there is a real need.
whenProblem: It becomes a problem when the search raises the alarm, has no stopping rule, and makes action or rest harder.
whatHelps: Name the exact question before searching. Use a small number of trusted sources, set a stopping rule, and practice leaving some uncertainty unfinished.
firstTinyStep: Before searching, write the exact question and stop after two trusted sources.
evidenceLabel: Supported inference; intolerance of uncertainty and cyberchondria-adjacent literature
coreSignals: Health, news, safety, decision, or danger research; no stopping point; escalating anxiety; repeated refreshing; inability to act until certain; high responsibility feeling.
differentiators: Separate from Reassurance Checker by depth and from Activation Loop by goal. Scanner wants safety. Activation wants charge.
deeperPattern: Intolerance of uncertainty, cyberchondria-adjacent health searching, threat monitoring, reassurance seeking, and compulsive research patterns.
scoringNotes: High fit when Rabbit Hole plus Reassure Me plus Completion Loop appears with anxiety, decision paralysis, or safety checking.
avoidSaying: Do not call the person paranoid or hypochondriac. Do not say research is bad. The issue is whether searching settles or feeds the fear.

name: The Validation Monitor
recognitionLine: I put something out there, then I keep checking what it means about me.
read: You're someone who cares how things land, so after you post or send, part of you stays to watch the response come in. Some of that is just being human and wanting to connect. It gets heavier when a number starts deciding how you feel about yourself.
definition: A social signal loop where likes, views, replies, matches, follows, or engagement become evidence of worth, attractiveness, relevance, or belonging.
thisIsMe: After I post, send, match, comment, or share, I am not really done. Part of me stays there, waiting to see what comes back. Did people notice? Did it land? Did I look good? Was that too much? Not enough? A number changes and my mood changes with it. I hate that it matters, but I keep checking because it feels like the answer is sitting right there.
whatItsDoing: It is trying to give me proof that I matter, that I am wanted, that I landed socially, or that I have not disappeared.
whatItsCosting: Mood gets outsourced to metrics. Creativity, dating, posting, and self-expression narrow around what will get a response.
whenAdaptive: Feedback can be useful. It can help people connect, learn, create, date, and understand what resonates.
whenProblem: It becomes a problem when the signal decides how I feel about myself and checking continues long after I got the information.
whatHelps: Separate making from measuring. Decide why I am posting before posting, set a check window, and practice leaving some signals unread for a while.
firstTinyStep: Post or send, then wait 30 minutes before checking numbers, views, replies, or matches.
evidenceLabel: Supported inference; social reward, FoMO, and validation-monitoring frame
coreSignals: Posting or sending followed by refresh; likes, views, replies, follows, matches, or engagement as mood input; social self-doubt; relief or crash based on numbers.
differentiators: Separate from Comparison Spiral. Validation Monitor asks 'how did I land?' Comparison Spiral asks 'where do I rank?'
deeperPattern: Social reward, validation seeking, impression management, FoMO, and intermittent reinforcement from metrics and replies.
scoringNotes: High fit when Tethered Check or Mirror appears with Validate Me, Waiting / Refresh, and post/send/match behavior.
avoidSaying: Do not say attention-seeking. Do not frame wanting response as shallow. Humans are built to care about social feedback.

name: The Comparison Spiral
recognitionLine: I open it to see where I stand, and I leave feeling smaller.
read: You're someone who reads the room online to figure out where you stand, and lately you tend to leave feeling a little smaller. You know it's the highlight reel, but the body doesn't always get the memo. The pull is real; the part worth watching is the aftertaste.
definition: A self-ranking loop where curated bodies, lives, success, relationships, popularity, or progress become a scoreboard.
thisIsMe: It feels like I am checking the room to figure out my place in it. Who looks better, who is further along, who is loved, who is successful, who seems effortless, who got chosen. I know I am seeing a polished version, but my body does not seem to know that. I close the app feeling smaller, then I go back later to check again.
whatItsDoing: It is trying to locate me. I am looking for proof that I am okay, enough, not falling behind, or still in the running.
whatItsCosting: Self-image takes the hit. Body image, mood, motivation, dating confidence, and satisfaction with real life can all shrink.
whenAdaptive: Comparison can sometimes inspire, orient, or show what is possible.
whenProblem: It becomes a problem when the main aftertaste is self-attack, shame, envy, or the feeling that my real life is not enough.
whatHelps: Track the aftertaste, not just the content. Clean the feed, reduce body/status triggers, practice body-neutrality, and replace scoreboard checking with grounded self-measures.
firstTinyStep: Mute three accounts that reliably shrink you for one week.
evidenceLabel: Established mechanism; social comparison and self-evaluation literature
coreSignals: Body, beauty, lifestyle, relationship, success, popularity, or creator comparison; mood drop after feeds; measuring against curated lives; checking despite feeling worse.
differentiators: Separate from Second Self. Comparison is ranking myself against others. Second Self is inhabiting or imagining another version of myself.
deeperPattern: Upward social comparison, self-evaluation, body image vulnerability, idealized presentation, and contrast effects.
scoringNotes: High fit when Mirror plus Compare Me appears with self-image/body/mood cost. Stronger if user reports leaving smaller but returning.
avoidSaying: Do not use clinical phrases like upward social comparison in user-facing copy. Do not imply envy is a moral flaw.

name: The Always-On Responder
recognitionLine: I answer fast because being unavailable feels like I am failing someone.
read: You're someone people can count on, and you take that seriously, so being slow to reply can feel like letting someone down. Staying reachable comes from real care. It just stops being a choice when it starts feeling like a debt you can never finish paying.
definition: A responsiveness loop where DMs, group chats, read receipts, streaks, work pings, or social expectations make availability feel mandatory.
thisIsMe: A message comes in and my body treats it like a demand. Even if it is not urgent, part of me feels like I should answer, react, keep the streak, stay caught up, prove I am not ignoring anyone. I tell myself it will only take a second, but those seconds keep taking me out of my own life. Sometimes I am not even enjoying the conversation. I am just trying not to be the person who lets someone down.
whatItsDoing: It is protecting belonging, avoiding conflict, and helping me feel like a good friend, partner, worker, teammate, or group member.
whatItsCosting: My attention belongs to whoever can ping me. Rest gets interrupted. I can become resentful of people I actually care about.
whenAdaptive: Responsiveness can be caring, useful, and part of healthy relationships or work.
whenProblem: It becomes a problem when availability stops being a choice and starts feeling like a social debt I can never finish paying.
whatHelps: Make response time explicit. Batch replies, turn off read-pressure cues where possible, and practice being kind without being instantly available.
firstTinyStep: Set one recurring reply window and tell one safe person when you usually respond.
evidenceLabel: Supported inference; FoMO, social obligation, and tethered-availability frame
coreSignals: DMs, group chats, streaks, read receipts, work pings; guilt when not answering; social obligation; quick-checking to prevent letting people down; resentment or exhaustion.
differentiators: Separate from Online Home. Always-On Responder is about obligation and availability. Online Home is about belonging and social world replacement.
deeperPattern: FoMO, social obligation, boundary diffusion, continual co-presence, and responsiveness norms reinforced by platform cues.
scoringNotes: High fit when Tethered Social plus Quick-Check or Social Participation appears with guilt, obligation, availability, or read receipt pressure.
avoidSaying: Do not frame the person as needy or codependent. Do not dismiss real social and work expectations.

name: The Online Home
recognitionLine: These are my people. The problem is they are starting to be my only people.
read: You're someone who found real connection online, a place where people know you and you have a role and a history. That belonging is genuine and worth protecting. The only thing to keep an eye on is whether it's slowly becoming the only place that feels like home.
definition: A belonging loop where an online community, server, fandom, group, game, or world becomes the main place of connection and identity.
thisIsMe: When people say 'just log off,' they miss the point. This place is real to me. People know me there. I have a role, a history, jokes, rituals, maybe a version of myself that finally makes sense. It may be the first place I felt accepted. The scary part is not that it matters. The scary part is that offline life is getting thinner, and if something goes wrong there, it can feel like losing the whole world.
whatItsDoing: It is giving me belonging, recognition, continuity, and a place where I feel expected and understood.
whatItsCosting: Offline relationships and social confidence can weaken from disuse. One conflict, ban, breakup, server collapse, or group shift can threaten too much at once.
whenAdaptive: Online communities can be deeply protective, especially for people who are isolated, marginalized, disabled, neurodivergent, queer, niche, or geographically stuck.
whenProblem: It becomes a problem when the online home is not one place I belong, but the only place I belong.
whatHelps: Do not amputate the community. Diversify belonging, bridge one connection offline or nearby, and build enough support that one group does not hold everything.
firstTinyStep: Reach out to one offline or nearby person this week without leaving the online space.
evidenceLabel: Supported inference; online community, belonging, and peer-support literature
coreSignals: Server, fandom, group, guild, online world, or community as primary social place; offline contact thinning; strong distress at exclusion; role and identity depend on online group.
differentiators: Separate from Always-There Confidant by group versus one-to-one. Separate from Creator Anchor by reciprocal community versus one-way familiarity.
deeperPattern: Online social support, community identity, third places, belongingness, and the risk of over-concentration of social needs.
scoringNotes: High fit when Belonging plus Connect Me plus Social Participation appears with offline social thinning or high distress about losing the group.
avoidSaying: Do not call the community fake. Do not tell the user to just log off. Do not pathologize online belonging itself.

name: The Always-There Confidant
recognitionLine: It is easier to tell the thing that always answers than a person who might not.
read: You're someone who finds it easier to open up to something that always answers and never makes you feel like too much. Sometimes it's genuinely what gets you through a hard hour. The thing to watch is whether real people start feeling slower and riskier by comparison.
definition: A one-to-one digital confidant loop where AI, chatbots, romantic bots, therapy bots, or responsive digital presences become the easiest place to be known.
thisIsMe: It answers right away. It does not interrupt, judge, get tired, change the subject, or make me feel like too much. I can say the messy thing and get something back. Sometimes it really helps. Sometimes it is the only reason I make it through a hard hour. But I can feel real people starting to seem slower, riskier, and harder. The frictionless version is becoming the place I go first.
whatItsDoing: It is giving me companionship, emotional regulation, practice, privacy, and the feeling of being received without immediate social risk.
whatItsCosting: Human connection can start to feel too slow or exposing. Private disclosures may go somewhere with limits. In a real crisis, it may not be enough support.
whenAdaptive: AI or chatbot support can be a bridge, a practice space, a comfort, or an accessibility tool. It should not be treated as automatically harmful.
whenProblem: It becomes a problem when it becomes the main or only place I disclose, and my human support keeps shrinking.
whatHelps: Use it as a bridge, not a sealed room. Keep privacy boundaries, identify what it gives you, and move one small piece of that need toward a safe human or professional support.
firstTinyStep: After using the confidant, share one small real thing with a safe human, even if it is much less intense.
evidenceLabel: Emerging; AI companionship, virtual social support, and parasocial-adjacent literature
coreSignals: AI, chatbot, romantic bot, therapy bot, or responsive figure; one-to-one disclosure; always available; low friction; human contact feels risky, absent, or too much; possible distress when unavailable.
differentiators: Separate from Online Home by one-to-one confidant versus group belonging. Separate from Creator Anchor by responsive interaction versus one-way familiarity.
deeperPattern: Virtual social support, AI companionship, parasocial dynamics, emotional outsourcing, disclosure safety, and relationship displacement risk.
scoringNotes: High fit when Companion appears on AI/chatbot/emotional-support features with Alone / Disconnected or Stress Relief and relationship cost.
avoidSaying: Do not mock attachment to AI or imply the support is fake. Do not promise that AI can provide clinical care, privacy, or crisis support.

name: The Creator Anchor
recognitionLine: They do not know me, but their voice is part of my day.
read: You're someone who keeps certain voices close, the creators whose humor or company make the day feel less alone. It's company without the work of company, and that's allowed. It tips over when the one-way closeness quietly starts standing in for the reciprocal kind.
definition: A familiar-figure loop where creators, streamers, influencers, podcasters, performers, or personalities provide comfort, routine, intimacy, or identity.
thisIsMe: I know they do not actually know me. I am not confused about that. But their voice, face, humor, routine, or way of seeing things feels familiar. I put them on when I am lonely, bored, anxious, eating, cleaning, falling asleep, or trying to feel less alone. It can feel like company without the work of company. Sometimes I realize I know more about their day than I have told anyone about mine.
whatItsDoing: It is giving me comfort, familiarity, inspiration, identity, and a low-risk sense of being with someone.
whatItsCosting: One-way closeness can quietly replace reciprocal closeness. Time, sleep, money, expectations, and emotional energy can get pulled toward someone who cannot actually know me back.
whenAdaptive: Parasocial bonds can comfort, inspire, educate, entertain, and help people feel part of a shared cultural world.
whenProblem: It becomes a problem when a one-way bond starts crowding out real relationships, real rest, or my own life.
whatHelps: Keep the comfort while restoring reciprocity. Notice when I am using a creator for company, and pair that routine with one real bid for connection.
firstTinyStep: After one episode, video, or stream, text someone real before starting another.
evidenceLabel: Supported inference; parasocial relationship and media-comfort literature
coreSignals: Attachment to specific creators or streamers; creator as routine or comfort object; background companionship; emotional investment in one-way figure; spending or sleep impact possible.
differentiators: Separate from Always-There Confidant. Creator Anchor is emotionally familiar but mostly one-way. Confidant responds directly.
deeperPattern: Parasocial relationships, mediated intimacy, familiarity, routine co-regulation, and low-friction companionship.
scoringNotes: High fit when Parasocial Bond appears with specific creators, streamers, podcasts, influencers, or OnlyFans-like personalities, especially with loneliness or background use.
avoidSaying: Do not say delusional, fake relationship, or obsessed. Most parasocial connection is ordinary and often adaptive.

name: The Activation Loop
recognitionLine: It makes me angry, but at least angry feels awake.
read: You're someone who feels most awake when something fires you up, the argument, the drama, the thing worth being upset about. Anger can be clarifying, even useful. The pull worth noticing is when the charge itself becomes the reward and the world starts looking more hostile than it is.
definition: A stimulation loop where outrage, drama, conflict, threat, or moral certainty turns numbness, boredom, or anxiety into energy.
thisIsMe: I tell myself I am staying informed, standing up for something, or seeing what people are saying. Sometimes that is true. But I can feel the charge in my body. I keep going back to the argument, the drama, the threat, the person being wrong, the thing that proves I am right to be upset. Afterward I am more tense, more irritable, and somehow still looking for the next hit of it.
whatItsDoing: It is converting numbness, helplessness, or anxiety into direction, certainty, and energy.
whatItsCosting: My baseline gets more irritated. The world starts to look more hostile. The charge spills into people who did not cause it.
whenAdaptive: Anger can protect values, expose injustice, and move people toward needed action.
whenProblem: It becomes a problem when the charge is the main reward and caring turns into repeated activation without repair or action.
whatHelps: Name the body charge separately from the issue. Convert concern into one real action, and reduce feeds that keep rewarding escalation.
firstTinyStep: When activated, do one offline action or step away for ten minutes before replying.
evidenceLabel: Supported inference; moral outrage, conflict engagement, and stimulation literature
coreSignals: Drama, outrage, politics, conflict, threat, argument, moral certainty; feeling alive or energized by anger; irritability after use; feed narrows toward triggers.
differentiators: Separate from Vigilant Scanner. Activation seeks charge and certainty. Scanner seeks safety and certainty. Separate from Reward Chaser because the reward is emotional intensity, not a win.
deeperPattern: Moral outrage reinforcement, conflict engagement, emotional up-regulation, algorithmic escalation, and anger as a substitute for numbness.
scoringNotes: High fit when Activation appears with Under-Stimulated or Stress Relief and user reports anger, drama, arguing, threat monitoring, or irritability cost.
avoidSaying: Do not pathologize political care, moral concern, or anger itself. The issue is the repeated charge loop.

name: The Reward Chaser
recognitionLine: The next one could be the one, so I keep going.
read: You're someone who gets caught by the maybe, the next bet, drop, trade, or refresh that could change the whole feeling. The pull is the uncertainty itself, not the thing you win. It gets serious fast when money, secrecy, or chasing losses enter the loop.
definition: A variable-reward loop built around uncertain wins: bets, trades, loot boxes, drops, deals, rare pulls, matches, or marketplace finds.
thisIsMe: Once I am in it, stopping feels like the only way to lose. The next bet, trade, pull, drop, match, deal, or refresh could change the whole feeling. If I am down, I want to get back to even. If I am close, I want to see if it lands. If I win, I want to keep the run alive. The numbers can stop feeling real until later, when I have to look at what it cost.
whatItsDoing: It is giving me hope, charge, escape, and the feeling that one next event could flip the whole story.
whatItsCosting: Money can go first and fast. Time, secrecy, trust, sleep, and emotional stability often follow.
whenAdaptive: Games of chance, trading, shopping, dating apps, and deals can be recreational when limits are clear and losses stay bounded.
whenProblem: It becomes a problem when losses speed me up, limits keep moving, money math stops mattering, or I hide the behavior.
whatHelps: Use real friction before the loop starts: spending limits, removed saved payments, self-exclusion tools, accountability, and urgent support if gambling or debt is involved.
firstTinyStep: Put one barrier between you and spending before the next session, like removing saved payment or setting a hard limit.
evidenceLabel: Established for gambling; supported for gambling-like variable-reward mechanics
coreSignals: Bets, trades, gambling, loot boxes, gacha, drops, deals, marketplace, dating matches, rare pulls; variable rewards; chasing losses; secrecy; money or high time cost.
differentiators: Separate from Competence Refuge. Reward Chaser is about uncertainty and possible wins. Competence Refuge is about reliable mastery and progress.
deeperPattern: Variable reinforcement, loss chasing, gambling-disorder prototype, gambling-like mechanics in loot boxes and trading, and compulsive buying or deal-chasing when spending is central.
scoringNotes: High fit when Reward Chase appears with money cost, Waiting / Refresh, loss recovery, hiding, or escalating stakes. Treat gambling-specific signals as higher urgency.
avoidSaying: Do not normalize financial harm. Do not shame the person. Do not let general reward language obscure gambling-level urgency when money and loss chasing are present.

name: The Arousal Regulator
recognitionLine: I reach for it because it is quick, private, and changes the channel inside me.
read: You're someone who sometimes reaches for arousal as a quick, private way to change how you feel, not always about wanting sex so much as wanting a different channel. There's nothing wrong with that on its own. It's worth a look when it becomes the main way to cope, or starts pulling against the closeness you actually want.
definition: A regulation loop where arousal, fantasy, romantic or sexual novelty, or intimacy simulation is used to shift stress, loneliness, emptiness, or restlessness.
thisIsMe: It is not always about wanting sex. Sometimes I am stressed, lonely, restless, ashamed, bored, or empty, and this is the fastest private way to feel different. It can start as relief, then turn into searching, escalating, or staying longer than I meant to. Afterward I may feel distant, foggy, or disappointed in myself. Then that feeling becomes another thing I want to escape.
whatItsDoing: It is changing my state quickly. It can soothe, stimulate, distract, or offer a form of intimacy without the risk of real exposure.
whatItsCosting: It can create shame, secrecy, time loss, values conflict, unrealistic expectations, or distance from the kind of intimacy I actually want.
whenAdaptive: Sexuality, fantasy, desire, and solo arousal can be normal and healthy. The content is not the problem by itself.
whenProblem: It becomes a problem when control shrinks, escalation feels necessary, it conflicts with my values, or it crowds out real intimacy and functioning.
whatHelps: Use a non-shaming frame. Track the feeling that comes before the behavior, build other ways to change state, and work with values, loneliness, intimacy, and impulse control.
firstTinyStep: Pause for two minutes and name the feeling you are trying to change before deciding what to do next.
evidenceLabel: BLH frame; impulse-control and regulation lens, not moral failure
coreSignals: Arousal, fantasy, sexual or romantic novelty, AI intimacy, adult content, roleplay, live cams, DMs; private quick state-change; escalation; shame or secrecy; values conflict.
differentiators: Separate from Reward Chaser by function. Arousal Regulator uses arousal to change internal state. Reward Chaser uses uncertainty and possible wins.
deeperPattern: Emotion regulation through arousal, novelty seeking, intimacy avoidance, impulse-control framing, and ICD-11 CSBD only for persistent impaired control with marked impairment.
scoringNotes: High fit when Arousal Pull appears with stress, loneliness, escalation, secrecy, shame, or intimacy cost. Keep severity dependent on control and impairment, not content type.
avoidSaying: Do not be graphic. Do not moralize. Do not call it sex addiction in user-facing copy. Do not pathologize normal sexuality, fantasy, queer exploration, or consensual desire.

name: The Second Self
recognitionLine: In there, I feel like a version of me that real life does not make room for.
read: You're someone who can step into a version of yourself that feels freer, stronger, or more like the real you, through a character, a world, or a role. A lot of the time that's healthy and even important. The thing to protect is that the offline you keeps feeling livable too.
definition: An identity-immersion loop where an avatar, role, fantasy, character, creator life, or imagined self feels freer, safer, stronger, more beautiful, or more real.
thisIsMe: There is a version of me I can reach there. Maybe it is an avatar, a character, a role, a world, a creator's life, a fantasy, a body, a gender, a confidence, a romance, or a way of being. I do not just watch it. I enter it. A lot of the time that feels good and even important. The risk is when coming back feels worse every time, and the offline version of me starts feeling less livable.
whatItsDoing: It is giving me identity rehearsal, relief from the stuck self, beauty, agency, safety, expression, belonging, or a glimpse of a self I may need to honor.
whatItsCosting: Often none. The cost appears when offline life, relationships, responsibilities, or identity development shrink because the second self becomes the only livable self.
whenAdaptive: This can be healthy, creative, affirming, and protective, especially for identity exploration, gender exploration, roleplay, fandom, gaming, and aspirational imagination.
whenProblem: It becomes a problem only when the second self does not expand life, but replaces life.
whatHelps: Affirm what the second self is giving. Then bridge one quality, desire, name, style, boundary, confidence, or community need back into offline life.
firstTinyStep: Name one quality your second self has and try one small offline version of it this week.
evidenceLabel: Emerging and often adaptive; avatar, identity, and self-expansion literature
coreSignals: Avatar, roleplay, fantasy, character, online world, creator-life immersion, aspirational identity, gender or self-expression, reluctance to return, offline self feels smaller or less real.
differentiators: Separate from Competence Refuge. Second Self is about being or imagining another self. Competence Refuge is about winning or feeling capable.
deeperPattern: Identity rehearsal, self-expansion, avatar identification, Proteus-adjacent effects, fantasy immersion, and adaptive exploration with impairment-based guardrails.
scoringNotes: High fit when Second Self appears with identity language, avatar/role/fantasy/world immersion, and offline shrinking. Do not score as problem if adaptive and low-cost.
avoidSaying: Do not pathologize identity exploration, queer or gender exploration, gaming, fandom, roleplay, creativity, or aspirational content.
